discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional quantum materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees collapses the Dirac bands into nearly flat minibands, where Coulomb interactions dominate kinetic energy. Jarillo-Herrero's group (2018) realised this, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in a single, gate-tunable carbon device. The work created twistronics: moire materials have since revealed orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Chern insulators, Wigner crystals and, in twisted MoTe2, the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect. For the first time, the strongly correlated phase diagram familiar from cuprates can be mapped continuously with a gate voltage in one sample, and probed by transport, scanning tunnelling and nano-infrared methods alike. Few recent discoveries have so quickly become a platform that the whole community has taken up, or reshaped how we design and control quantum matter.
